the problem of testing the equality of two mean functions or of two covariance operators of functional data.
testing the equality of the mean functions or covariance operators of two functional random variables in the framework of functional data analysis.

the bootstrap method performs well in finite samples.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bootstrap-based functional tests have good size and power, but they are not always as good as the corresponding nonparametric tests.
bootstrap-based testing is a useful and practical approach to testing the equality of functional mean and covariance structures.
bootstrap methods can be used for testing equality of covariance operators in a functional data setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for functional data, the bootstrap method is a viable alternative to the classical resampling methods for testing hypotheses.
, in the absence of a closed-form expression for the limiting distribution of the test statistic, a bootstrap-based approach can be used to construct tests that perform well in finite samples.
bootstrap-based testing of equality for mean functions or covariance operators can be a powerful tool for functional data analysis.
